 British citizen among six killed in Poland shooting as three more bodies found at gunman's home
 7 November 2026 Summary
 This live page has now closed - read more in our news story 
 A British citizen is among six people killed in the Krakow shooting, the head of Poland's police force says 
 Marek Boroń says three Polish citizens were also killed, with two yet to be identified - 16 people were injured in the attack, including the suspect, two police officers and five foreign nationals
 Speaking at the same press conference , Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk says three more bodies were found at the suspect's home, which authorities continue to search
 Poland's interior minister said earlier the suspect - a 25-year-old Polish citizen - is believed to have been inspired by "far-right ideologies" , while police said he used "military weapons" in the attack
 A 24-year-old university student told our reporter that he pulled his girlfriend and her "petrified" parents into a hotel to hide during the attack
 Video shows gunshots ringing out in Krakow's Main Market Square; images show emergency services at the scene

 Live Reporting
 Edited by Kieran Kelly, with Magda Mis reporting from Krakow
 Six killed in Krakow shooting, as three more bodies found in gunman's home published at 23:06 GMT 7 November 23:06 GMT 7 November 
 Freya Scott-Turner 
Live reporter 
 Image source, AFP via Getty Images At around 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow, southern Poland, a gunman drove onto the city's main square and began "firing at random people from his car", as described by police.
 Six people were killed in the attack, including a British citizen, alongside three Polish victims, and two people who are yet to be identified.
 Sixteen were injured - that includes the suspect and two police officers. Five foreign nationals from Britain, Germany, Austria, Portugal and Russia were also injured, the interior ministry told Reuters.
 We have since learnt that the suspect is a 25-year-old Polish citizen, who police say wore "military-style attire" and used "military weapons" in the attack. More weapons were found in his vehicle. 
 The suspect held "very radical views" , with everything indicating that he was inspired by "far-right ideologies", according to Poland's interior minister. 
 Prime Minister Donald Tusk later said searches were ongoing at the suspect's home, where authorities had found the bodies of a man and two women believed to be members of his close family. 
 As authorities continue to investigate this tragedy - mass shootings are rare in Poland - tributes have been laid at the scene at Main Market Square, Krakow, where a period of mourning has been declared. One eyewitness of the attack told the BBC that he's "alive, maybe not well, but alive". 
 We're now ending our live coverage, but you can read more about this in our news story

 Foreign Secretary pays tribute to British national and other victims of shooting published at 22:52 GMT 7 November 22:52 GMT 7 November 
 Image source, PA Media Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband says the UK government "deeply mourns the British national and other victims" who died in the shooting in Krakow.
 He says in a statement: "All of my deepest condolences go to the families of the victims.
 "The UK stands resolutely in solidarity with the people of Poland."

 What authorities are still trying to establish about the Krakow shooting published at 22:38 GMT 7 November 22:38 GMT 7 November 
 Jacob Phillips 
Live reporter 
 Image source, EPA/Shutterstock A British citizen is among six people killed in the Krakow shooting, Polish police say, with three more bodies found at the suspected gunman's home.
 "It looks like they are members of his close family," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk told a news conference. 
 Here's what authorities are still investigating:
 Officials were asked if the suspect was collaborating with any groups or paramilitaries - authorities confirmed the attacker was not a soldier and that there is only one suspect at this stage
 However, Tusk also said at the news conference he was "convinced" that authorities would be able to "very quickly" detain "possible supporters of the perpetrator" 
 Earlier Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said everything indicated that the suspect was inspired by "far-right ideologies" and held "ultra-nationalist views". Kierwiński said this needed to be verified
 Kierwiński said one hypothesis was that the guns used in the attack came from the 25-year-old suspect's family home. Officials are investigating where the weapons came from and if the suspect had a licence to use them
 Authorities are still working to identify two of the victims that were killed in the shooting. Earlier the commander-in-chief of Poland's police Marek Boroń said three victims were identified as Polish citizens and one as British 
 Polish police are still working at the scene of the attack and speaking to witnesses, Boroń added

 Watch: People run for cover as police chase takes place during Krakow shooting published at 22:33 GMT 7 November 22:33 GMT 7 November 
 Footage from this afternoon shows people running for cover in a street in Krakow as shots ring out.
 Around a dozen people are seen running inside two buildings before a black car with its front window open is followed by a police car. 
 Media caption, People run away from gunshots in Krakow
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We were hearing gunshots, a lot of people were screaming' published at 22:26 GMT 7 November 22:26 GMT 7 November 
 Freya Scott-Turner 
Live reporter 
 Cezary, a 24-year-old university student in Krakow, was waiting for a taxi with his girlfriend and her family just off Krakow's main square at around 15:00 local time (14:00 BST).
 "We were talking about the ordinary stuff, the new job that I got," he tells me. "Suddenly we started to hear some noises... Shots, something like that." 
 At first they thought it was related to some rowdy football fans that had been in the city the day before, but when they reached the corner of the square they saw four bodies. 
 "And we were still hearing gunshots, a lot of people were screaming," he says, adding that he saw someone trying to resuscitate a person covered in blood on the ground. 
 Many people, including his girlfriend's parents, were "petrified" and "standing and looking straight", he says, describing how he pulled them into a hotel to hide. 
 Image source, Courtesy of Cezary Image caption, Cezary, 24, had been having lunch with his girlfriend's family in Krakow's Main Market Square
 Cezary says the whole ordeal was "very quick", lasting maybe two to three minutes. 
 They managed to get away from the area when the taxi arrived - with the driver seemingly unaware of the ongoing attack: "We were saying to him, 'okay man, just drive, just get out of here'."
 He plans to stay inside at his girlfriend's tonight and has let his friends know on social media that he's "alive, maybe not well, but alive".

 'True heroes': Tusk names two police officers injured in shooting published at 22:07 GMT 7 November 22:07 GMT 7 November 
 Image source, Getty Images Prime Minister of Poland Donald Tusk has named the two police officers injured in the Krakow shooting as senoir constables Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański.
 They are "true heroes" who "likely saved many lives, without regard for the risk of losing their own". 
 "Their condition is serious, but they are receiving excellent care," he adds. "All of Poland is rooting for you."

 Warsaw implements additional security measures after Krakow shooting published at 21:55 GMT 7 November 21:55 GMT 7 November 
 Police in Warsaw say additional security will be implemented following the shooting in Krakow. 
 Additional patrols took place across the capital Warsaw, located about 300km from Krakow, shortly after today's shooting. 
 Large crowds were placed under surveillance, Warsaw police say, with road barriers to be implemented at the entrances to streets leading to Krakowskie Przedmieście, one of the most-visited streets in the capital. 
 "Until the causes of the tragic attack in Krakow are established, heightened precautions can be expected as services carry out their daily work to maintain security in Warsaw," a spokesperson says.

 Burnham 'shocked and saddened' by 'appalling' shooting published at 21:15 GMT 7 November 21:15 GMT 7 November Breaking 
 Image source, Reuters Prime Minister Andy Burnham says he is "shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting in Krakow today". 
 "My thoughts are with the families of those who have lost their lives, everyone injured and all those affected by this senseless violence," he says. 
 "The United Kingdom stands in solidarity with the people of Poland."

 Three bodies found at suspect's home, Tusk says published at 21:09 GMT 7 November 21:09 GMT 7 November Breaking 
 We can now bring you more from the press conference with Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk.
 He says he can confirm that the bodies of two women and one man have been found at the suspect's home.
 He says "it looks like they are members of his close family". 
 Media caption, Three bodies found at suspect's home, Polish PM says
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Authorities searching home of suspect and his family, Polish PM says published at 21:04 GMT 7 November 21:04 GMT 7 November 
 Image source, Getty Images Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk says authorities are searching the house of the suspect and his family.
 "There could be quite a lot of arms, quite a lot of guns in this house," he says. 
 He says searches are also ongoing to check whether the suspect's car is a threat and could explode.
 Tusk says he is "convinced" that authorities will be able to "very quickly" detain "possible supporters of the perpetrator", and that the police and others will give information to the public on this "as quickly as possible".

 Officers exchanged fire with gunman three minutes after first reports, police say published at 20:58 GMT 7 November 20:58 GMT 7 November 
 Image source, EPA/Shutterstock Image caption, Marek Boroń (R), the head of Poland's national police, spoke at a briefing in Krakow this evening
 Polish police officials are giving further updates on the attack.
 The head of Poland's police service Marek Boroń says officers exchanged fire with the gunman three minutes after they received reports of the attack, which came in just after 15:30 local time (14:30 GMT).
 Two police officers have undergone surgery for their injuries, with Boroń calling for thoughts and solidarity with them and their families.
 About 30 teams of officers were deployed to assist, he adds.

 British citizen among six killed in shooting, Polish police say published at 20:48 GMT 7 November 20:48 GMT 7 November Breaking 
 A British citizen is among six people killed in the Krakow shooting, the commander-in-chief of Poland's police, Marek Boroń, says.
 Three victims were Polish and one British, he says, adding that two are yet to be identified.

 Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk is speaking to reporters at a news conference.
 We will bring you the latest updates shortly - you can also watch live at the top of the page.

 Residents to be evacuated as suspect's car is searched, police say published at 20:28 GMT 7 November 20:28 GMT 7 November 
 Polish police say residents in an area near where the car driven by the suspect remains will be evacuated as investigations continue.
 "The perpetrator’s car, located at the intersection of Dietla and Stradomska streets, is being checked for pyrotechnic devices," Krakow police says in a statement.
 Officials are also appealing to the public for any information including recordings they have that could assist in investigations.

 Gunman behind Krakow shooting may have been inspired by far-right ideology - recap published at 20:11 GMT 7 November 20:11 GMT 7 November 
 Jacob Phillips 
Live reporter 
 Poland's interior minister says initial indications suggest the gunman who killed six people in Krakow today was influenced by "far-right ideologies" - here's what else we learned during the news conference:
 Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz began the press conference by describing the incident as a "terror attack" and explained that a policeman who stopped the suspect in his tracks remained in critical condition 
 Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said police shot towards the attacker three minutes after they were first called about the attack
 He confirmed that six people were killed in the shooting, including one foreign national 
 Some 16 were injured in the attack, Kierwiński said, including the suspect, five foreign nationals and two police officers 
 Kierwiński explained that the suspect was shot and remained in a serious condition 
 The interior minister added everything indicated the suspect was inspired by "far-right ideologies" and indications showed he held "ultra-nationalist views". Kierwiński said this needed to be verified.
 One hypothesis is that guns used in the attack may have come from the suspect's family home 
 Media caption, 'Attacker had very radical views,' Polish interior minister says
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Five foreign nationals among those injured - interior minister published at 20:07 GMT 7 November 20:07 GMT 7 November 
 Answering another question, Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński explains that 16 people were hospitalised across Krakow following the attack, with medical procedures ongoing.
 As a reminder, Kierwiński said earlier that two people had been released from hospital. 
 He says that five of those injured in the attack are foreign nationals. Kierwiński said earlier that one of those killed was a foreign national. 
 Kierwiński is also asked about the number of shots that were fired by the suspect during the attack.
 The interior minister says "many shots have been fired" but he can not provide any more information.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Suspect may have taken guns from family home, minister says published at 19:38 GMT 7 November 19:38 GMT 7 November Breaking 
 Answering a question from a reporter, Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński says one hypothesis is that the guns used in the attack were taken from the suspect's family home.
 Kierwiński says several guns are registered by the suspect's father but it is "too early" to say.
 He adds that the first analysis indicates that the suspect had "ultra-nationalist views", which Kierwiński says needs to be verified.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Indications suspect was inspired by 'far-right ideologies', says interior minister published at 19:29 GMT 7 November 19:29 GMT 7 November Breaking 
 Image source, EPA/Shutterstock Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński says the suspect in the attack has been "shot and neutralised" by police and remains in hospital in a serious condition.
 He says that he is undergoing a second operation.
 Kierwiński says there are no reasons to believe there was more than one attacker.
 The interior minister adds that it looks like the attacker held "very radical views" and that in the car he was driving "many guns were found", with searches still being carried out.
 He says the suspect is a Polish national who is 25 years old and that his home is being searched.
 Kierwiński says everything indicates he was inspired by "far-right ideologies".
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Very quick' police reaction prevented 'much bigger massacre' - interior minister published at 19:26 GMT 7 November 19:26 GMT 7 November Breaking 
 Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński follows the defence minister in urging citizens not to share disinformation, explaining that footage which appears online can cause panic.
 Kierwiński then praises the "very quick" reaction of police who prevented what could have been a "much bigger massacre".
 He says the policemen shot at the direction of the attacker three minutes after they received a call about the attack, and that the fire service and ambulances were also at the scene after three minutes.
 Kierwiński says "this terrible act of terror killed six people" and explains four people have been identified, with work ongoing to identify two more. He says their families will be informed. 
 The interior minister says one foreign individual is among the four killed who have been identified.
 He explains that 16 people were injured, including two police officers and the attacker. Two people have since been released from hospital. 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Polish defence minister denies reports that suspect was a soldier published at 19:22 GMT 7 November 19:22 GMT 7 November Breaking 
 Image source, EPA/Shutterstock Polish Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz begins the press conference by describing the incident as a "terror attack" and passing on his condolences to all the victims.
 He asks for people to maintain unity and says there are many people in hospital fighting for their lives, including a policeman who prevented the shooter from continuing his attack.
 He asks people to not share disinformation and denies reports that the suspect was a soldier in the Polish Armed Forces.
